about: The ecosystem's budgets, as data (Bet 3; decisions W1 to W24). `project` is what `vlx build` holds an application to when its valance.json sets none (W14). `framework` is what the release check holds the reference applications and the runtime to (scripts/check-budgets.mjs, over the output of scripts/measure-footprint.mjs). Brotli bytes, because that is what travels (W2).
rule: A ceiling is the baseline plus 5 percent, rounded up to the next 100 bytes (the next 10 under 1,000), then ratcheted down (W3). A ceiling above that needs `analysis`: the path of a size analysis that says why (W23a), and a decision row. The check refuses a raised ceiling without one.

project.note: W14: the framework's own start-up ceilings. `initial` warns above the largest reference application's JavaScript and CSS ceiling (docs-app) and fails at twice that; `runtime` is the WebAssembly runtime, the same for every application, so a growth of it fails the build of whoever upgrades.

ceilings.what: Counter application, everything the browser transfers, brotli
Client JavaScript each added page costs, raw

ceilings.note: W24: the 1,000-update heap gate stays off
ratcheted down: W21 fixed the growth, the memory is flat

exact.what: Bytes a PORT is sent for one changed item of 1,000 rows, as patches

ratios.what: Counter, time until a click is handled, unthrottled
Counter, time until a click is handled, 4x CPU

known.what: Bytes a PORT is sent for one changed item of 1,000 rows, whole tree
known.reason: the Desktop protocol sends the whole tree on every update; patches are Bet 3's own work item, not WP8

known.what: The newest published @valancex set, with the release being measured, installs together
known.reason: Was red from MESH 0.16 until VALANCE 0.14: NEXUS 0.14 and PORT 0.12 stopped their MESH peer range at 0.15. With --tree the release candidate's own tarballs stand in for the published VALANCE packages, so a release is held to installing beside the newest of the others before it is published (a published VALANCE, the previous release, would gate a release on its predecessor)
